subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: developer-view.ts:19-20 is explicitly DB-import-free ('PURE module — no @/lib/db import, because every Developer component is a client component') and developer-view-load.ts's getDeveloperView() runs server-side, called from page.tsx:56-59 (a Server Component) which passes the resolved DeveloperView as props. No browser-held DB credential and no broker route relaying an upstream failure exist in this context, so every technique's precondition (client-held credential, or a broker reporting an upstream failure) fails to hold.

subjects.subject: remediation-handoff
subjects.evidence: src/lib/org/playbook-brief.ts:5-27 (playbookMarkdown) is a deterministic, self-contained single artifact (title, dimension, summary, checklist steps, explicit 'Ask') meant to be pasted into a developer's own local coding agent Ascent cannot observe — realizes single-artifact-prompt-construction. src/lib/db/playbooks.ts:184-215 stampPlaybookApplications marks a playbook adopted ONLY when (a) it was IN THE loop lane's brief the agent actually saw, and (b) a real rescan verified the close ('the agent's claim is not the trigger — the verifier is') — a precise, well-anchored realization of evidence-based-auto-close that specifically guards the coincidental-close failure mode the golden path names as the subject's hardest problem.

subjects.subject: wizard-flows
subjects.evidence: Playbook authoring is a single prefillable form seeded from PLAYBOOK_TEMPLATES (src/lib/org/playbook-templates.ts:14-19) with no sequence of dependent decisions converging on one commit — the golden path itself names exactly this shape ('a form wearing pagination... if every step could be shown at once with no loss of meaning, show them at once') as the canonical non-wizard case. 'Steps' in this context names checklist items inside the generated artifact (playbook-brief.ts), not UI wizard steps — the matcher's why=["apply","steps","flows"] looks like a lexical collision on that word, not a real match.

subjects.subject: remediation-handoff
subjects.evidence: handoff/route.ts realizes handoff-tenancy-and-idempotence: requireOrgAccess + whole-request 403 on any foreign/unknown id (no existence oracle), PUBLIC_ORG refused, MAX_BATCH 50, only open->in_progress with skipped-and-why reported. Wave-3 item 8 closed the one gap: db/scans-recommendations.ts handoffRecommendations now does ONE membership-scoped read and per-row CAS (status+org in the WHERE) in one tx with events+audit, so a row moving open->done mid-request can no longer be silently reopened. Residual tension: the ownership predicate now has two spellings (getRecommendationOrgSlug and the batch read's join), both in the same module.

subjects.subject: agent-memory
subjects.evidence: This context (src/app/api/org/skills/*, org/tokens) is a versioned skill-CATALOG — promoting a generated SKILL.md into an org library, gated by plan entitlement (promote/route.ts:1-13,43-55) — with no recall/decay/consolidation of retrieved knowledge across agent turns anywhere in it. None of agent-memory's techniques (memory-value-model, recall-injection, decay-and-forgetting, consolidation, coverage-instrumentation, baseline-ladder) have a precondition that holds here; the actual memory system (recall.ts/decay.ts/org-memory-lifecycle.ts) is a separate context ('Org Knowledge & Skills/Org Memory') already judged conformant in the map. This reads as a matcher lexical collision on "skills"/"library"/"generated" rather than a real match — worth a coverage-question note to the registry rather than a technique-level verdict.

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: github/source.ts:375-377 interpolates raw String(e) into a GitHubError relayed verbatim (stream/route.ts:367 -> useReportScan.ts:292); on a GHES base a malformed URL publishes the internal API host.

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: src/lib/register/data.ts:117-144 REGISTER_REPO_SELECT is a structural Prisma select carrying no sensitive/internal columns, and isPrivate is re-asserted at the scan query, the repo query, AND per-row in registerEntryFrom:155 — three independent checks, matching omit-the-column-not-the-value's structural-exclusion discipline; leaderboard/page.tsx:61 and portfolio.ts:80-82/32 degrade every DB or authorization failure to null/empty via .catch(()=>null) rather than surfacing a raw error, matching opaque-upstream-errors' spirit for a public surface. Separately noted (not scored as a technique deviation): leaderboard/page.tsx:98-101 renders getDbMode()/dbModeLabel() ('Served live from Aurora DSQL') to every anonymous visitor of this crawlable public page — the SAME value api/health/route.ts:29-38 explicitly reasons 'describes deployment TOPOLOGY... shouldn't be handed to an anonymous caller' and gates behind CRON_SECRET. I did not mark this a deviation because it discloses only a coarse backend-family label (no hostname/credential/error-body), and the codebase treats it as a deliberate trust-building UI element (also on the landing page, IndexGallery.tsx) rather than an oversight — but it is a real inconsistency in how the project applies its own stated topology-disclosure rule, worth registry attention.

subjects.subject: plan-entitlements
subjects.evidence: src/lib/plans.ts:80-444 is the single tier model every surface reads (id-vs-label split lines 26-31, decideScanCharge/decideCharge naming unlimited/allowance/credit/denied lines 348-409, selfHosted() short-circuit at planAllows:439-444) and src/app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts realizes lifecycle revocation end to end (ENTITLING_SUB_STATUSES grace :52, retainedHigherPlan downgrade guard :70-73, proportional refund clawback :222-251, stale-paid fence :162-183) — the model, gate, page and webhook agree by construction.

subjects.subject: rate-limiting
subjects.evidence: rate-limit.ts:60-63 trusts x-real-ip under the default hops=1 on the operator's word alone — no runtime witness (cf. the VERCEL gate the technique's exemplar uses) — so an unconfigured self-hosted deploy lets a caller mint a fresh bucket per request; :373-385 also spends per-IP allowance on globally-refused requests. Refusal contract, reaper, and basis labels are all realized. (2026-08-30: public-scan-quota's read-decide-write tx moved into db/scan-quota.ts — quota policy unchanged; the deviation above is untouched by it.)

subjects.subject: cost-metering
subjects.evidence: scan/stream/route.ts has neither credit gate (route.ts has 6) yet asserts 'token scans are credit-metered'; webhook/route.ts:313 rescans unreserved; debits never pass scanId/actor, so spend is unjoinable.

subjects.subject: plan-entitlements
subjects.evidence: entitlement.ts:72-84 computes orgExists 'so a caller can 404 a phantom slug'; no production caller reads it - all three gates return 402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, so a deleted org is told to buy credits it has.

subjects.subject: cost-metering
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:59-76 isBillableScan is the ONE billable predicate shared by the chart/CSV/gate paths (comment names the drift bug this prevents); byRepo/byLane/byTeam (lines 111-129) carry multi-axis attribution and estimatedCostUsd/costBasis (102-110) is null rather than a fake price when unpriceable — realizes usage-ledgers, spend-attribution and spend-observability for the reporting surface. Enforcement techniques (budget-enforcement, preflight-estimation, reversible-debit-and-settle) are not-applicable here — this context is the read/reporting side; the gate is Credits & Entitlements, judged separately with a recorded deviation.

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/client.ts reads DATABASE_URL/DSQL config via plain process.env, never NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed, and src/lib/db/index.ts:4 imports "server-only" so a client-component import of the DB barrel fails the build by design (comment cites ADR 2026-08-28-server-only-boundary); env.ts documents the NEXT_PUBLIC_ split explicitly. Prisma/DSQL is reached exclusively server-side — there is no browser-held credential or RLS-style policy engine fronting this store (unlike Supabase, which is deliberately regime-one for auth only, per supabase/client.ts:1-4 and .env.example:145).
